speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Given the sudden onset lasting only 3 minutes, lack of hearing loss on your initial report, and the absence of neurological deficits, this fits the classic presentation of BPPV rather than Meniere's disease or a stroke. We can confirm this with the upcoming MRI and hearing tests, but are you currently experiencing any dizziness when you roll over in bed or look up?
